clue.text: Football club accepts what manager did in foreign capital

indicators.note: a club that accepts something takes it in, so these letters go inside the club's letters

parts.note: a manager ran the business or team

explanation.surface: A football club welcomes a manager's efforts in some foreign city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like a city but is money: the franc was the currency of France and is still used in Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: A currency used abroad is foreign money, and capital is another word for money.

clue.text: Plant recreated such an interior for timeless Italian car

indicators.note: the letters become the interior for, the inside of, the car
timeless means without T, the abbreviation for time

parts.note: Fiat is an Italian car maker

indicators.note: recreated means made anew, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A plant whose bloom recreated the colourful interior of a classic Italian car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'timeless' means without T, the abbreviation for time; 'recreated' is the anagram signal and 'interior for' puts the result inside what is left of the car maker.
explanation.definitionFit: Fuchsia is a flowering shrub with hanging blooms, so an example of a plant.

clue.text: Jazz fan can help irate trumpeter!

indicators.note: to jazz something up is to liven and change it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A jazz enthusiast can assist an angry trumpet player.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a jazz musician, but the trumpeter trumpets through its trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: This animal trumpets loudly with its trunk, so it is literally a trumpeter.

clue.text: Relative taking care of you and me at home

parts.note: c/o is the postal abbreviation for care of
you and me together are us
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A family member who looks after us both in our own house.
explanation.definitionFit: The child of an aunt or uncle is a family member, a kind of relative.

clue.text: Old rocking chair put in empty attic

indicators.note: one set of letters is put in the other, placed inside it
an empty word keeps only its shell, the outer letters, with its contents removed
a rocking chair moves about, so these letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: An old rocking chair is stored in a bare loft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocking' looks like part of the furniture but is the anagram signal; 'empty' keeps only the attic's outer letters, and 'put in' places the jumbled chair between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something archaic belongs to an earlier age, a synonym for old.

clue.text: Pack boot of car in service area

indicators.note: to pack is to fill, so the serve's letters are packed round the letter

parts.note: an ace is a winning serve in tennis

indicators.note: a car's boot is at its rear, so this takes the word's last letter

explanation.surface: Instructions to load a car's boot at a motorway service station.
explanation.walkthrough: A boot is the British word for a car's trunk; a service area is a motorway rest stop. 'service area' splits into a tennis serve and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a unit of land measurement, so a measure of area.

clue.text: Knight's path is an L, in welcome change introduced by chess principally

indicators.note: this piece comes first, introducing the rest
principally means first and foremost, so this takes the word's first letter

parts.note: hi is a word of welcome

indicators.note: the letter goes in the middle of the other word

parts.note: to vary is to change

explanation.surface: In chess, a knight moves in an L shape, a pleasant novelty for a beginner.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about a chess knight's L-shaped move; the definition means a knight's code of conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: Chivalry is the code of honour knights followed, their path or way of life.

clue.text: Fare for passage? Quite the opposite!

definitions.text: Fare for passage? Quite the opposite!

parts.words: Fare for passage? Quite the opposite
parts.note: not money paid for a journey, but a passage for fare, a tube that food travels along

explanation.surface: Querying the price of a voyage, then reversing the idea.
explanation.walkthrough: Fare reads as a ticket price but means food; reversing the phrase gives a passage for food.
explanation.definitionFit: The digestive tract runs from mouth to anus, the route food travels through the body.

clue.text: Its detonation involved leader of revolutionary government and CIA

definitions.text: Its detonation involved leader of revolutionary government and CIA

indicators.note: a detonation blows things apart, so these letters are scattered into a new order
the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The CIA plotted an exploding smoke against Cuba's revolutionary leader, Fidel Castro.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: the CIA reportedly planned to kill Castro with a booby-trapped smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: The CIA's alleged plot against Castro involved an explosive roll of tobacco, which he famously smoked.

clue.text: Disaster apparently related to small branch closing

parts.note: a -y suffix turns stick, a small branch, into an adjective meaning stick-like
a closing is the end of something

explanation.surface: A catastrophe linked to a local office being shut down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'branch closing' suggests a business office shutting, but branch is a twig and closing is an ending.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to come to a nasty, unpleasant finish is to meet ruin or disaster.

clue.text: Lap dancing in a ring? That's foremost way to get fit

parts.note: a lap of a track is one circuit

indicators.note: the foremost letter of a word is its first one
dancing letters move about into a new order

explanation.surface: Lap dancing in a boxing ring, offered as the best way to get in shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges IN A RING plus T, the first letter picked by 'That's foremost', into TRAINING.
explanation.definitionFit: Circuit training is an exercise regime of rotating stations, a method of building fitness.

clue.text: Brief success extinct, once Essex town is abandoned

indicators.note: letters that are abandoned are left behind, taken out of the words

parts.note: taken as written: an English county
T is a standard abbreviation for town

explanation.surface: A short remark that success has died out once a place in Essex is deserted.
explanation.walkthrough: Essex is an English county east of London. Taking ESSEXT out of SUCCESSEXTINCT leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Brief and to the point are synonyms for concise, wasting no words.

clue.text: Rush job

definitions.meaning: to rush is to hurtle along at speed
a profession or line of work followed over a lifetime

explanation.surface: A two-word instruction to hurry up with some work.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to move headlong; as a noun it means a working life or profession.

clue.text: Throw up Liverpudlian stew

parts.note: to lob is to throw something up high
Scouse is the nickname for anything from Liverpool, its dialect and people

explanation.surface: Someone vomits after eating a Liverpool stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw up' suggests vomiting but means toss in the air. Scouse is the name for Liverpool's people and dialect, from this very dish.
explanation.definitionFit: This sailors' meat and vegetable dish, long eaten in Liverpool, is a kind of stew.

clue.text: Spotty coverage in area of East London on phone network

indicators.note: heard over the telephone, so the word is taken by its sound alone

parts.note: Hackney is a borough in East London

explanation.surface: Questions about how patchy mobile signal is in part of East London.
explanation.walkthrough: Hackney said with a Cockney dropped H, as it would be in East London ('in' sets this up), sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The skin condition covers the face with pimples, so it is a covering of spots.

clue.text: He shouldn't be trusted with editing their copy

indicators.note: editing a text changes it about, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A man warned off from altering someone's written material.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who preaches what he doesn't practise is a fraud, someone untrustworthy.

clue.text: Warning about Bow being short of ecstasy and heroin?

indicators.note: the shortened word goes about, around, the other piece
being short of something means lacking it, so the letter is removed

parts.note: a notice can be a warning, as in notice to quit
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
a bow is shaped like an arc

explanation.surface: A caution that the London district of Bow is running low on drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow is an area of East London; here it is a curve. 'heroin?' ends with a question mark as it defines by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Heroin is an example of an addictive, sleep-inducing drug, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Those leading accurate radius curvature lenses supply clarity

indicators.note: read as the adverb of supple, flexibly, so these letters bend into a new order
the letters leading the following words are their initials

explanation.surface: Optical lenses ground with precise radius of curvature give a sharp image.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' is not the verb but 'in a supple way': it rearranges ARC (initials picked by 'Those leading') with LENSES.
explanation.definitionFit: Being easy to see through or understand is a synonym for clarity.

clue.text: Unpleasant matter is something to chew over, right?

indicators.note: the chewed food lies over, covering, the letter, so it goes inside

parts.note: cud is what a cow chews

explanation.surface: Asking whether some nasty substance is something to mull over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chew over' looks like one phrase meaning ponder; split it, 'over' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Crud is slang for dirt or filthy gunk, an unpleasant substance.

clue.text: Detect underground particle accelerator

parts.note: Dis is the Roman underworld, the realm below ground
CERN is the European physics lab housing the Large Hadron Collider

explanation.surface: Finding the subterranean collider beneath the Swiss-French border.
explanation.walkthrough: CERN's Large Hadron Collider really is underground, which makes the surface read naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: To discern something is to notice or perceive it, a synonym for detect.

clue.text: Minister conveyed by bicycle rickshaw

indicators.note: conveyed by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A priest is carried along in a pedal-powered rickshaw.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister of religion is a member of the clergy, a churchman.

clue.text: Look forward to Bar overturning limits on censorship

indicators.note: overturning flips a stretch round so it reads the other way

parts.note: bar as a preposition means except

explanation.surface: Anticipating a pub turning against the limits of censorship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limits on censorship' are C and P, its outer letters; 'overturning' swaps their places in the stretch C-E-P of the synonym for bar.
explanation.definitionFit: To expect something is to anticipate it, looking ahead to its coming.

clue.text: Principle relating to race repulses Nationalist

indicators.note: repulses means drives away, so the letter is removed

parts.note: ethnic means relating to race or culture

explanation.surface: A racial principle is rejected by a nationalist politician.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes the Nationalist the subject; in fact the race word repulses, drives out, its N.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethic is a moral standard or rule of conduct, a synonym for principle.

clue.text: Doctors backing Republican Party achieve success

indicators.note: this piece backs onto, sits behind, the other one

parts.note: GOP, the Grand Old Party, is the nickname of the US Republican Party
to doctor a drink is to lace it with something

explanation.surface: Physicians supporting the Republicans do well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctors' looks like physicians but is a verb: doctors a drink, laces it.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: someone who will go places is bound to succeed and do well.

clue.text: Name faculty in report

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: sight is one of the senses, a faculty

explanation.surface: Identifying members of a university faculty in an official report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faculty' suggests a university department but is a bodily sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To cite someone is to mention them by name, as in a report or citation.

clue.text: What makes conditions better and speeds up complaints procedures for customer?

definitions.text: What makes conditions better and speeds up complaints procedures for customer?

parts.words: What makes conditions better and speeds up complaints procedures for customer
parts.note: conditions and complaints are illnesses; a policy pays for treatments and gets operations done sooner for the policyholder

explanation.surface: A service that improves terms and handles customer grievances quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conditions', 'complaints' and 'procedures' read as business terms but are medical: ailments and operations.
explanation.definitionFit: Private medical cover pays for treatment and lets the policyholder skip waiting lists.

clue.text: Ignored lice all over skin

parts.note: to cut someone is to ignore them pointedly

indicators.note: all over the place means scattered, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone paid no attention to lice crawling all over their skin.
explanation.definitionFit: The cuticle is the layer of dead skin at the base of a nail, so a kind of skin.

clue.text: Gutsy piece by company performing around London's West End

indicators.note: in an across word the west end is the leftmost, first letter

parts.note: an actor who is on is performing on stage

explanation.surface: A brave theatre piece by a troupe on stage in London's theatre district.
explanation.walkthrough: London's West End is its theatre district, which suits the surface; here it is just the word's first letter, L.
explanation.definitionFit: The large intestine is part of the guts, so a piece of them, with gutsy a pun on brave.
